label: input b at original positions 1-3
explanation: Fires exactly when the input token is b at original-phase steps 1, 2 or 3 (every such step fires; precision 1.0, recall ~0.999 on dev). Magnitude depends on position: strongest at t=1 and t=2 (about 0.87-1.0 of max, top examples are all j b ...), weaker at t=3 (about 0.36-0.47 of max, so t=3 carries only ~16% of the mass despite a similar count). Does not fire on b at t=0 or t>=4, on any other token, at the delimiter, or on copy-phase inputs (apart from ~40 stray activations at t=5). Not modulated by previous tokens, first token, or L.

issues: Minor wording: the explanation says the feature does not fire 'on copy-phase inputs' but also mentions about 40 stray activations at t=5. Those 40 (31 on test) are all copy-phase steps in L=3 sequences where b is fed back as copy input at t=5 (recalling original position 1), with tiny activations of 0.04-0.12 of max. They carry 0.0% of the activation mass. This is noise, not a systematic class.

Minor: 'previous tokens have no real effect' holds for firing but not for magnitude. Every max-activation example has prev token j at t=1, so prev_tok slightly modulates magnitude. Firing rate is flat across prev_tok, first_tok and L.

All factual claims verified. Test: precision 1.000, recall 0.9994, F1 0.9997, mass recall 0.9999, 0 false positives on dev and test. t=3 alone has mass recall 0.161 and recall 0.330, which matches the claim of about 16% of mass from a similar number of activations. No activations at t=0, t=4, t>=6 or the delimiter, and none on any token other than b.
